learning.title: Negated closing keywords still link unfinished issues for closure
learning.trigger: A partial delivery PR explains that its parent must remain open.
learning.mistake: Used negated closing phrases in PR prose. GitHub still populated closingIssuesReferences with unfinished parents. Correcting only the hosted body let a publisher restore the unsafe phrase from its older local input.
learning.rule: Write "keeps #N open", not "does not close #N" or "must not close #N". Bind partial delivery to a genuinely scoped child issue with native parent and real dependency relationships. Reserve positive closing-keyword syntax for the completed intended child.

verification.requirement: Correct both the hosted body and local publication input or template. Read back the final body and actual closingIssuesReferences; intended meaning alone is not proof of GitHub linkage.
Check closure references again during final merge admission. Unfinished parents must be absent. Diagnose persistent linkage rather than assuming a body edit removed it immediately.
Refresh publication hashes and body/comment readback after prose changes. Preserve unchanged-source review, tests, captures and running CI; do not fabricate a new source run for metadata-only work.

learning.boundary: A child issue does not waive a real dependency or remove the parent's remaining acceptance criteria. Record the actual dependency reasoning and retain incomplete parent requirements. Serialize publication ownership so stale writers cannot undo the correction.
